general_information.Syllabus Name: E-Customs_Khai báo hải quan điện tử
general_information.Learning-Teaching Method: - Offline.- Research-Based Learning (RBL) integration:Selected topics in this course are delivered using a lResearch-Based Learning (RBL) approach. Rather than converting the entire course into a full research-based subject, the course integrates one focused RBL mini-module in Unit 6 (E-Customs Procedures and Documentation), where students investigate declaration errors and documentary inconsistencies, analyze evidence, propose corrective actions, defend their decisions, and reflect on compliance implications. This design supports inquiry-driven learning, evidence-based reasoning, academic defence, and reflective practice while remaining feasible for a technical, application-oriented course in Semester 5.
general_information.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_information.Description: This course provides specialized and applied knowledge of electronic customs declaration and customs compliance in global logistics and supply chain operations. It equips students with the legal, technical, and procedural foundations required to understand customs administration; apply HS classification (Harmonized System Codes Classification), customs valuation, origin-related preferential treatment, and tariff/tax rules; and prepare and review e-customs declaration logic, supporting documents, and declaration flows for standard import/export and selected customs regimes. Through scenario-based learning, guided discussion, document review, and case analysis grounded in FIATA (International Federation of Freight Forwarders Associations) and VLI (Vietnam Logistics Research and Development Institute) resources, students develop compliance awareness, professional responsibility, and practical decision-making skills relevant to customs, freight forwarding, and international logistics environments. - AI Tools will be used to support students in: (1) generating ideas/structures for their speaking notes and slide structure of important topics of the course. (2) editing the slide set after students have already finished it.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible for preparing assigned materials before class, participating actively in in-class discussions and activities, and submitting all individual and group assignments on time. - Laptops may be used in class only for academic purposes under lecturer guidance. - Students should access the institutional LMS/portal regularly for announcements, materials, and assignment updates. - Students are expected to work professionally in group activities and respect academic integrity in all assessed tasks.
general_information.Tools: Internet; institutional FLM; presentation software; spreadsheet software for practice; AI-supported learning tools as directed by the lecturer
general_information.Note: AI Policy: Students may use generative AI and other digital tools only as guided by the lecturer for idea generation, concept clarification, drafting support, document checking, and learning enhancement. Any AI use in assessed coursework must be disclosed clearly and students remain fully responsible for the accuracy, legality, and originality of their submissions. AI use is not permitted in quizzes and the final examination unless explicitly authorized. Students must verify AI-generated content against official customs/legal sources and comply with academic integrity standards.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain the role of customs administration, trade compliance, and the legal-institutional framework governing e-customs operations in Vietnam within the context of global logistics and supply chain management.
Apply HS classification principles to determine appropriate tariff headings for typical traded goods and justify classification decisions using product information and legal notes.
Apply customs valuation, origin-related preferential treatment, tariff rules, and tax principles to determine customs value and payable import taxes in common customs scenarios.
Prepare and review the logic, data fields, supporting documents, and procedural steps of electronic customs declarations for standard import/export and selected special customs regimes.
Analyze customs compliance risks, liabilities, documentary errors, penalties, and professional responsibilities of customs declarants, brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics enterprises.
Use digital tools and AI responsibly to support customs learning, document preparation, and professional decision-making while maintaining academic integrity and ethical standards.
